name: Disorder of Phospholipids, Sphingolipids and Fatty Acids Biosynthesis with Central Nervous System Predominant Involvement
aliases: Phospholipid and Sphingolipid Metabolism Defect with Neurological Manifestations

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for CNS-Predominant Lipid Biosynthesis Disorders

criteria.description: Presence of progressive neurodevelopmental delay or regression with predominant central nervous system involvement
Abnormal plasma or CSF phospholipid, sphingolipid, or fatty acid profiles consistent with biosynthesis defects
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes involved in phospholipid, sphingolipid, or fatty acid biosynthesis pathways
MRI evidence of CNS white matter abnormalities or cerebral atrophy supportive of diagnosis
Exclusion of other metabolic or neurodegenerative disorders by appropriate testing

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria (clinical neurological features, biochemical lipid profile abnormalities, and genetic confirmation) must be met for diagnosis.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including neurology, genetics, and metabolic testing.

searchTerms: severe low muscle tone in central body

pathognomonic.symptomName: Cerebral white matter abnormalities on MRI
pathognomonic.notes: Visible as diffuse hypomyelination or demyelination
searchTerms: abnormal brain white matter on MRI
white matter changes in brain imaging

common.symptomName: Seizure disorders including generalized tonic-clonic seizures
Visual impairment due to optic nerve involvement
searchTerms: vision loss from optic nerve damage
poor eyesight due to nerve problems

occasional.symptomName: Mild cognitive impairment in early stages

laboratory: Elevated plasma lysophosphatidylcholine and abnormal sphingolipid profiles
Increased very long chain fatty acids in plasma
imaging: MRI showing diffuse cerebral white matter hypomyelination
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes such as PISD, SPTLC1, or ELOVL family genes
Confirmed autosomal recessive or dominant inheritance patterns
other: Abnormal enzyme activity assays related to lipid biosynthesis in fibroblasts
Electrophysiological studies showing slowed nerve conduction velocities

distinguishingFeatures: Predominantly white matter involvement but without characteristic lipid biosynthesis enzyme defects
Different genetic mutations and biochemical profiles
Presence of elevated very long chain fatty acids but with additional systemic involvement such as adrenal insufficiency
Distinct biochemical markers and genetic mutations

redFlags: Rapid neurodevelopmental regression in infancy or early childhood
Unexplained seizures with white matter abnormalities on MRI
references: Orphanet: Disorder of phospholipids, sphingolipids and fatty acids biosynthesis with CNS predominant involvement (ORPHA:352306)
